::: {.callout-note}
**This page is for the facilitator.** It is rendered with the site but left out of the navbar, so nothing on the site links to it. The track pages under `tracks/` are participant-facing and contain no instructor guidance, which is collected here. The run sheets are the facilitator guides of the [housing-audit case](housing-guide.qmd), the [EU-frames case](eu-frames-guide.qmd), the [immigration-and-trust case](trust-guide.qmd) and the [cohabitation case](cohabitation-guide.qmd).
:::

## The formats

The facilitator chooses the format, the case and, for a one-day workshop, the focus of a course; participants do not choose, and the opening page describes the formats without offering a choice. Each track is an ordered route through pages that already exist on the site, with a docked sidebar of its own (`_sidebar.yml`) and a slides page embedding the deck it runs on. Name the track of a delivery in `delivery.track` of `_variables.yml`, and the callout of the opening page links it; the navbar then shows a participant the last track page that they opened. The decisions behind the formats, and the order in which their material is being built, are in `_planning/formats-2026-10-27.md`.

| Format | Case | Track | Deck |
|---|---|---|---|
| Short session, browser only | housing audit | `tracks/housing-short/` | `slides/housing-short.qmd` |
| One day, open science | housing audit | `tracks/housing-one-day-open-science/` | `slides/housing-one-day-open-science.qmd` |
| One day, data tools | housing audit | `tracks/housing-one-day-data-tools/` | `slides/housing-one-day-data-tools.qmd` |
| One day, methods | housing audit | `tracks/housing-one-day-methods/` | `slides/housing-one-day-methods.qmd` |
| One day, open science | EU frames | `tracks/eu-frames-one-day-open-science/` | `slides/eu-frames-one-day-open-science.qmd` |
| One day, data tools | EU frames | `tracks/eu-frames-one-day-data-tools/` | `slides/eu-frames-one-day-data-tools.qmd` |
| One day, methods | EU frames | `tracks/eu-frames-one-day-methods/` | `slides/eu-frames-one-day-methods.qmd` |
| Three days | immigration and trust | `tracks/trust-three-days/` | in preparation; the one-day deck `slides/trust-one-day.qmd` meanwhile |
| Three days | cohabitation | `tracks/cohabitation-three-days/` | in preparation; the one-day deck `slides/cohabitation-one-day.qmd` meanwhile |
| Three days | EU frames | `tracks/eu-frames-three-days/` | in preparation; the deck of the earlier three-day course `slides/eu-frames-three-days.qmd` meanwhile |
| Self-study | the four cases | `tracks/self-study/` | the decks of the cases |

**What each one-day focus keeps.** The open-science day takes the paper, the five analysts, the estimand statement, the reproduction of one reanalysis chosen by each participant and the replication with new data, and ends on what a preregistration fixes, with the block read and filled in but not run; it has no menu, no class chart and no submissions. The data-tools day practises R, the IDE, a Quarto report, data management and version control on the data of the case, with the reproduction as the target that the code works towards; it has no menu, no class chart and no submissions. The methods day puts the robustness exercise at the centre: the menu, the class chart with its submissions, the curve of the claim and the declared analysis. All three are taught mainly in the browser lab of the case, with the workspace as an option for those who have installed R.

## The browser labs

Each case has a browser lab, a page that runs R in the tab of the browser and holds the five tasks of the exercise beside the workspace. The labs of the housing-audit and EU-frames cases are live: they load the data of the case, which are small (about 100 KB of emails, and a panel of 43 KB), and run the code of the tasks on them, each fit in a fraction of a second, so the short session and the one-day workshops are taught in them. The labs of the immigration-and-trust and cohabitation cases are demonstrations. Those cases are taught over three days, in which every participant installs R and works in the workspace, and their labs fit no model: every result is read from small tables that the pipeline of the case writes with the code of the workspace, and each sits beside that code, so the lab and the workspace give the same numbers. A demonstration lab still sends both submissions to the class chart, so a participant whose machine fails can follow the tasks and submit, but cannot fit a specification of their own; the cohabitation lab runs the reproduction of Task 3 in full, on the file of the analysts. In all four labs the causal-graph task prints the answers that the pipeline computed with dagitty for the graphs that the cell offers, because dagitty cannot run in the tab; any other graph goes to the workspace.

## The decks

The decks of every case are assembled from one pool of segments: the case-neutral segments of `slides/_segments/shared/` and the segments of each case in `slides/_segments/<slug>/`, whose setup chunk comes after the shared one and gives the shared segments the addresses of the case. A deck is a list of `{{< include >}}` lines with its own agenda, aims and part dividers.

**How the optional runs are switched.** In the segment files, every slide of an optional run is marked with `.deepdive` and a `run` attribute (`tools`, `r`, `methods`, `multiverse`). A deck lists the runs that belong to its main flow under `core-runs:` in its YAML, and `slides/core-runs.lua` strips the `.deepdive` mark from those headings, so `nav-tools.html` neither hides them on the `d` key nor badges them as optional. A run that is not listed stays optional: it is hidden in lean mode and has the escape-hatch link on its first slide.

**Why no segment is included twice in one deck.** The segment files contain R chunks with labels, and knitr refuses a duplicate label, so each deck includes each segment at most once.

**Rebuilding a deck.** Edit the segment files for content, or the deck file for order and framing, and render the deck on its own (`quarto render slides/housing-short.qmd`). A change to a shared segment needs every deck that includes it rendered again (`grep -l "shared/_x.qmd" slides/*.qmd`). The project render fails at its final move step on this machine, so decks are rendered one at a time.

## The housing-audit case

The housing-audit case is taught in a short session and in one day. The short session runs in the browser lab alone, in two halves of about seventy-five minutes: nothing is installed, nothing is sent to the class chart and nothing is preregistered. The three one-day focuses are taught mainly in the browser lab, with the workspace as an option. In Task 3 each participant chooses which of the analysts to reproduce; the four who recorded a statistic reproduce exactly from the public file, and P9W8Y, who recorded none, can be rerun but not matched. The [run sheet of the case](housing-guide.qmd) has the timings of the short session and of each focus of the day, the expected numbers, the checks before the day and the order of what to cut.

## The EU-frames case in one day

The one-day workshops of the EU-frames case work on the country-year panel alone, with the methods that it needs, and nothing from the respondent files. In Task 3 participants choose among the analyses that worked on aggregate data; the analyses of KEVF1 and PRL47, which work on respondents, belong to the three-day course.

**Pages that every focus shares.** Every track starts from the [case study](../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd), which tells the original study, SCORE and Multi100, the five reanalysts with an assessment of their choices, and the conversion lesson on how Multi100 turned their statistics into one effect size. The specification menu is taught as the full set of fourteen decisions, on the [decision map](../cases/eu-frames/map.qmd) and the [specification menu](../cases/eu-frames/menu.qmd), with the curve of 864 specifications as the subset that an audit judged justifiable for this claim. The helpers of the browser lab and of the workspace refuse an option that is off the curve, with the one-sentence reason recorded in `data/menu_options.csv` and the page that teaches the option. Every result is classed by standard errors clustered by country with the CR2 correction and Satterthwaite degrees of freedom; the specification of C6HJR (t = −3.804, r = −0.242) has a CR2 p of 0.0504 on 9.8 degrees of freedom and is not significant under that rule, which is worth saying before anyone asks. The [run sheet of the case](eu-frames-guide.qmd) has the timings of each focus.

## Three days

The three-day courses take the immigration-and-trust, cohabitation or EU-frames case from its raw data. Day 1 introduces open research and its infrastructures, SCORE and Multi100, and the paper in detail, and ends with the tools installed and the raw data downloaded (the ESS Data Portal for the trust case, the files of the National Survey of Family Growth for the cohabitation case, the GESIS archive for the EU-frames case). Day 2 teaches R and the IDE on the data of the case, builds the analysis file from the raw files as the data-management training, and reproduces one of the five reanalyses, chosen by each participant, with a short report of the reproduction sent to the class. Day 3 turns to robustness: the estimand and the graph, the menu and the methods behind it, and an analysis of each participant's own design, preregistered, run and sent to the class chart.

The track pages are written to that design; the slides of the three days, the participant scripts that build the analysis files from the raw files, the reproduction of all five reanalyses of each case and the submission of a reproduced result are being built. Until the decks exist, the slides page of each track shows the one-day deck of the case (for the EU-frames case, the deck of the earlier three-day course).

**The discovery of the cohabitation case.** The file that Multi100 gave the analysts, from which the class reproduces the recorded tests, holds almost none of the marriages of 1995. Keep it for the reproduction on day 2: before then, point participants only to sections 1 and 2 of the case study and the claim of the exercise overview, because the later sections, the menu, the decision map, the multiverse page, the cheatsheet and section 3 of the event-history module tell the story.

## Self-study

The self-study track takes the four cases in the order of their difficulty, with the companion modules between them, so that each case adds the methods that the one before it did not need; a semester course can follow the same route in class. Its pages contain their own compression notes, written to the reader, because no facilitator is there to apply them. What the facilitator can still do for a self-study cohort is keep the live results pipeline running between deliveries, so that a result submitted alone appears on the Multiverse page of its case (`facilitator/live-results-setup.md`).

**The class charts.** Each case has a chart of its own on its Multiverse page, and each chart reads only the rows of its own case from the shared results Form. The labels of the housing-audit, immigration-and-trust and cohabitation cases carry the case word after the tag (`explore: [amber-otter-42] housing …`), while those of the EU-frames case keep the frozen format without one. Each workspace keeps its own tag in `.class-tag`, so ask a cohort to choose one nickname and to pass it as `nickname = "..."` in every case. A chart keeps the rows of earlier deliveries until the sheet is cleared.
